dossier.mechanism: One developer in Finland ships a family of single-purpose Apple apps that are private by construction and publishes each app's declared privacy data field by field (_data/transparency.yml); the studio site's job is to route a visitor to the one right app microsite fast and make the privacy claim checkable.
dossier.audienceScene: Mostly a phone visitor who arrived from Google or an AI answer on a journal post, guide or 'alternative to X' page, taps 'who makes this?' and lands on the home or /apps/ index needing one app fast; secondarily privacy-minded Apple users and indie iOS developers browsing the whole catalogue on a laptop in the evening, and press checking who is behind it.
dossier.culturalHome: Independent Apple software culture (one-person iOS/Mac developers, App Store privacy labels, App Tracking Transparency), European and Nordic everyday design and media, and the privacy movement's show-the-receipts ethic; the studio's own footer places it at 63°N, Finland, since 2025.
dossier.mustProve: In one viewport: this is one person's independent catalogue of distinct private apps, here is the fastest route to the one you need, and the privacy claim is a public per-app record (0 tracking domains, 0 ad SDKs, audited 11 Jun 2026), not a slogan.
dossier.categoryDefault: Indie studio homepage: serif or grotesk headline beside floating device mockups, a trust-stat row, then 2- or 3-column grids of equal app cards (icon, name, tagline, pills) per category, journal cards, FAQ, footer: exactly the incumbent v3 Paper & Ink.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Anti-design studio page: a stark plain-text or monospace list of app names in giant type on white or black (apps.txt / terminal brutalism), no imagery, no proof.
dossier.literalReading: 'Lager' (Swedish/German: stock, store, warehouse) + 'land' reads as a warehouse or stockroom of apps; the place read literally is Finland as aurora, snow, pine forest and sauna. Candidate 7 spends the name's literal reading once; the postcard reading of the place is spent nowhere.
evidence: _includes/footer.html already says 'Made on a MacBook at 63°N' and 'since 2025': the place and date are the studio's own words.

_data/transparency.yml: 19 rows, last_audit 2026-06-11; tracking false and 0 tracking domains on every row; third-party SDKs only in MediaKit (Unrar.swift) and Pawza (ZIPFoundation); AppMeta, Mockly and AppMeta Pulse use the visitor's own Apple ID / API key; AppMeta Pulse is 'manifest pending' (18 manifests + 1 pending).
19 live apps plus Tare (status upcoming, sitemap:false, no images); first release GymLogger X 2025-09-01, newest Xiangqiful 2026-09-30.
42 journal posts (2025-12-27 to 2026-10-01), 104 alternatives pages plus index, 4 /for/ audience pages plus hub, 5 guides.

assets/icons/lagerland-mark.png (stone 8-point star in a ring of stone blocks) is RGBA but has a grey/white transparency checkerboard baked into its pixels (corner pixel #D3D3D3, alpha 1): every style needs a clean vector redraw.

Seven icons (earnlock, liftlog, mediakit, pawza, rightsplit, soon, taskful-day) carry baked white rounded corners, and mediakit.png is 1740x1734 (not square): every style masks icons with an iOS squircle at about 1.06 overscale.
head.html loads GoatCounter (cookieless counting): studio copy must never imply the website itself is untracked; privacy claims stay per app.
The Smart App Banner is emitted only for layout:app; journal posts and guides whose mentioned_apps holds exactly one app could emit that app's banner (proposed in all three styles).
alternatives/index.html hard-codes numberOfItems 104 in its ItemList JSON-LD (contract says counts are computed).
Incumbent home: left serif headline with purple second line, floating device composition right, trust-stat row, then 2-column card grids per cluster: the template every style refuses.

candidates.name: Independent record label: spines, sleeves, catalogue numbers
candidates.why: The canonical model for one small house with many distinct artists: every sleeve is its own world, and the label appears only as a catalogue number and one constant mark. Formats map to platforms, the discography to the index, the album credits to the transparency record.

candidates.name: Räsymatto: the Finnish rag rug
candidates.why: Every Finnish home's striped rug, woven from strips of different cloth on one warp. Each app is a band in its own colours, and the shared warp threads (no tracking, no ads, no accounts) run through every band. True to the place without being literal.

candidates.name: Postage stamps and the first-day cover
candidates.why: Every stamp is a different artwork held by one constant format (perforation, denomination, issuer). The denomination carries price.value, the first-day postmark carries release.first_release, and sealed mail stands for privacy. Risks twee.

candidates.name: Orienteering map and control-description sheet
candidates.why: Finland's sport map (ISOM colours, magenta course overprint) is itself a routing system: courses of numbered controls by need. The IOF control-description table can carry each app's declared facts. Less known outside the Nordics.

candidates.name: Teletext: Yle Teksti-TV / Ceefax page 100
candidates.why: Europe's routing page: three-digit page numbers, the P100 index and four Fastext keys. A receive-only medium whose MIX mode lets each app's own picture show through one uniform text frame. Strong for Europeans, unknown to many US visitors.

candidates.name: 63°N daylight almanac
candidates.why: Turns the footer's own line into data: the year's day-length band at 63°N with each app pinned at its real release date. True chronology and true place, but weak at routing by need, and it sits near AfterShift's and Soon.'s time worlds.

candidates.name: Open depot: Lagerland as an open store (literal reading)
candidates.why: 'Lager' means store. Read literally, the name lifts from warehouse to the open-storage depot (Schaulager, Depot Boijmans), where a collection is kept in view, located by aisle-bin codes and labelled. That gives routing by location and proof by inventory. It spends the name's literal reading once.

styles.label: The Open Depot
styles.lineage: Open-storage art depots, where a whole collection is kept in view on racks and every object is located and labelled: Schaulager, Basel (Herzog & de Meuron, 2003) and Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam (MVRDV, 2021). Crossed with Nordic warehouse wayfinding: pallet-rack beam labels with aisle-bin codes, stencil aisle signs and stocktake cards. The name's literal reading (lager = stock, store) is spent here once and lifted from warehouse to open store.
styles.thesis: The catalogue is an open store, not a showroom. Every app sits in view at a fixed aisle-bin location with its declared contents on the label (tracking domains, SDKs, account). It refuses the hero-plus-icon-card grid by making the homepage the depot's location index, read aisle by aisle and picked by hand.
styles.scene: A visitor reads bin labels on a phone at midday, as if standing in a white-painted open depot under even 5000K high-bay light, with orange beams, blue uprights and labels legible at arm's length. Scheme: light.
styles.colorStrategy: Committed: beam orange carries about 30% of the surface as masthead, aisle beams and ledger header rows; blue uprights frame both page edges; concrete grey is the ground; each app's own colour appears only on its box front.

palette.role: label stock: bin labels, beam labels, reading sheet, QR quiet zone
stencil black: ink and headlines (14.3:1 on concrete, 4.7:1 on beam orange)
beam orange: rack beams and ledger header rows; black text only (white fails at 3.8:1)
upright blue: edge uprights, links (8.0:1 on concrete), focus ring
galvanised grey: secondary text and rules (5.0:1 on concrete)

type.display: Big Shoulders Stencil Display 800 and 500 (Fontsource, 14 KB per weight)
type.text: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 700 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 12-14 KB each)
type.utility: Martian Mono 400 and 600, only for real data: location codes, declared values, dates, counts (Fontsource, 10 KB each)
type.rationale: Depots and crates are marked with sprayed stencil, and the condensed stencil fits a seven-aisle directory on one beam; it is kept at 40px and above. Atkinson was drawn by the Braille Institute for legibility at distance and for low vision, which is the label-reading job and also a calm reading face. Martian's wide mono reads like label-printer output and is never used for running text. Total about 86 KB.

styles.conversion: Routing comes first. The aisle beam (seven jump labels) and the ledger rows are the action, and every row's app name links straight to /apps/<slug>/. The Pick drawer adds an orange pick-ticket button ('Go to Observa · 1-02') and the official App Store badge (Apple artwork untouched, 40px). On screens 1024px and wider it also shows assets/qr/<slug>.svg in a white label, 'Scan to install on iPhone'; Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The price statement is price.value verbatim on every row. The sticky bar: once the aisle beam scrolls away, a 44px orange beam with the seven aisle labels sticks to the top. Smart App Banner: none on studio pages, except journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons are squircle-masked at 1.06 overscale (cropping baked white corners) on a box front painted in the app's own world ground (studio_swatch from its chosen microsite). The bin label stays in constant studio type; the box belongs to the app.
visitorPath: Beam masthead: nav as white beam labels on the orange beam
Level one: stencil H1 and lede (the about-strip text, AI-canonical), then the stocktake strip (computed proof from transparency.yml)
Aisle beam: seven aisle labels (the 7 need clusters) as jump links

Location index: per aisle, a stencil sign plus the cluster lead line, then ledger rows (aisle-bin code, box front, name, tagline, platforms, price.value, declared tracking/SDK/account); each row opens a Pick drawer with screenshot, Go-to ticket, badge and QR
Goods in: the newest arrival (computed from release.first_release, now Xiangqiful) on the receiving bay: large box front, first screenshot, real arrival date
Swap shelf: four comparisons as transfer tickets ('From Strong → GymLogger X') plus the computed comparison count → /alternatives/
Delivery notes: the latest two journal posts (date in mono, title, lede)
Ledger extract: the 6-app transparency sample (orange header row, mono values) → /transparency/
Service counter: six FAQ <details> tags (first open), plus a founder line (Antti Aittamaa, one developer, Finland, since 2025) and email
Close: the aisle labels again, 'Pick something'
Footer: the depot floor plan, with aisles as outlined rectangles listing every app, plus studio links, privacy, support and 'Made on a MacBook at 63°N'
styles.navigation: The orange beam is the masthead on every studio page: the mark plus LAGERLAND label, then beam labels for Apps, Journal, Transparency, Alternatives and About, with Guides, For and Support in the 'Index' directory sheet (a <details> panel that works without JS). The current page's label is printed on blue with white text. Breadcrumbs are set as a location path in Martian ('LAGERLAND / JOURNAL / streaks-are-a-debt'). /apps/ is the full location index with each aisle's lead copy. /for/ pages are pick lists: the audience's stack as location rows, each with why it is on the list.
styles.signatureInteraction: Pick. Tap, click or press Enter on a ledger row and its box slides out of the bin: a drawer opens with the app's box front at large scale (app ground colour, 120px squircle icon, first screenshot 240px tall), the orange 'Go to <App> · code' ticket, the official badge and, on wide screens, the QR. Technique: each row is a <details> whose summary is the full ledger row; CSS transitions grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr, and the box lifts 6px with a soft 0 8px 24px shadow. On hover the box only nudges 3px as a preview; about 10 lines of JS close the previously opened drawer. No JS: <details> works natively, and every word (name, job, platforms, price, declared values, link) sits in the always-visible summary, so the drawer adds only image, badge and QR. Reduced motion: the drawer opens instantly with no lift.
styles.motionGrammar: Mechanical and short: things move along rails and never float or fade. Pick drawer 180ms ease-out; box lift 6px; aisle jumps use smooth scroll (instant under reduced motion); the sticky aisle beam drops in over 120ms. No reveal-on-scroll, no parallax, no count-up: stocktake values are static text.
styles.readModeVariant: Journal posts, guides, /for/ pages, transparency, the alternatives index, about, support and 404 keep the orange beam masthead and one blue upright as the left rail. On desktop the 28px upright's punched slots mark each H2, and the current section's slot fills orange: a working table of contents. On mobile the upright is 6px and an 'On this shelf' <details> holds the contents. The title is stencil 800 in sentence case at 56-72px; the meta line (date, read time, last updated) is Martian 14px. The column sits on a white label-stock sheet over concrete: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 18/1.6 at 68ch in #14191F, with H2s in Atkinson 700 at 26px. The Quick Answer is a bin label: a white panel with a 12px orange top band, titled 'Quick answer', the answer at 19px (speakable). Tables are ledgers: orange header row, black text, Martian figures, concrete zebra rows; plist keys are in Martian on concrete. Mentioned apps close the post as their ledger rows, with the Pick drawer. The journal index is a delivery-notes ledger: date, title, read time, and the location codes of mentioned apps. Guides are problem tickets that resolve to bins. /transparency/ is the full stock ledger, one bin label per app with every field in a dl and the source status printed as label text (Source-verified / App Store-declared / Manifest pending). The alternatives index is a ledger grouped by our app under stencil signs. 404 reads 'BIN EMPTY' above the aisle directory.
styles.assetsNeeded: A clean vector studio mark: an SVG redraw of the stone star and block ring, because the PNG has a baked checkerboard. Data, not art: a per-app studio_swatch {ground, ink} in front matter, sampled from icons now and replaced by each chosen microsite's ground later. Racks, beams and labels are CSS. Optional later: per-app SVG wordmarks from each microsite's face for the box fronts. Everything else runs on the existing icons, screenshots and QR SVGs.
styles.risk: It is the name's literal reading. A depot can read cold and industrial against 'calm', and a dense ledger can feel like a spreadsheet to a casual shopper if row rhythm and box fronts are not generous. Orange-and-blue racking also nears generic stock-photo industry. Stencil tires below 40px, so it never sets running text.
styles.memoryTest: The Lagerland site was an open warehouse: huge stencil aisle signs, orange shelf beams, and every app on a labelled bin saying what's inside (0 trackers, 0 ad SDKs). I pulled one out and its box showed me the app.

styles.label: The Back Catalogue
styles.lineage: Independent record labels as identity systems. Factory Records' catalogue numbering under Peter Saville: every artefact numbered, every sleeve its own design. The yellow-label principle of Deutsche Grammophon: one constant cartouche on radically different covers (principle only, none of its trade dress). And the record shop's browser shelf, with spines filed by genre behind black plastic divider cards.
styles.thesis: The studio is a small label. Each app is a record filed spine-out by genre in its own colours, and the label appears only as a catalogue number and one constant cartouche. It refuses the hero-plus-icon-card grid by making the catalogue a shelf you browse and pull a record from.
styles.scene: A browser at the new-releases shelf of a small record shop on a bright afternoon, the wall painted the label's cloudberry yellow, spines lit flat and even. Scheme: light, drenched.
styles.colorStrategy: Drenched: the cloudberry wall is the ground of every Persuade surface; black divider cards and type set the structure; the only other colours are the apps' own, on their spines and sleeves. Read pages keep the yellow as masthead band and put the column on inner-sleeve white.

palette.role: cloudberry: drenched wall/ground, Read masthead band
sleeve black: ink, headlines, divider cards, buttons (9.8:1 on cloudberry)
inner-sleeve white: reading sheet, cartouche, price stickers, QR quiet zone

type.text: Familjen Grotesk 400, 600 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 11-12 KB each)
type.utility: none: catalogue numbers, dates and prices are set in Familjen Grotesk 600 with tabular figures
type.rationale: Krona One is a semi-extended, low-contrast sans with the stance of mid-century Nordic label and advert lettering, wide enough to own a spine at 16px set vertically and a 72px H1. Familjen Grotesk, from a Stockholm studio, is compact with a high x-height, built for tracklists and calm enough for liner-note reading. Total about 45 KB.

styles.conversion: The shelf is the routing: every spine name links to /apps/<slug>/. The face-out sleeve carries a black 'Open <App> →' button, the price sticker (price.value verbatim), the official App Store badge (unaltered, 40px) and, on desktop, the app's QR printed where a sleeve's barcode sits, 'Scan to install on iPhone'; Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The back-cover discography repeats every route as text. The sticky bar: after the shelf leaves the viewport, a 48px black divider strip sticks to the top with the seven genre labels in yellow, jumping back into the shelf. Smart App Banner: only on journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons and names: the spine and sleeve wear the app's own world colours (studio_swatch from its microsite, interim sampled from the icon), with the icon squircle-masked at 1.06. The label adds only the cartouche and catalogue number, never its own colour, to an app's sleeve.

styles.navigation: Black divider-card tabs across the yellow masthead (Apps, Journal, Transparency, Alternatives, About; the current card is raised); Guides, For and Support sit in the footer and the mobile 'Catalogue' sheet (<details>, works without JS). /apps/ is the whole shelf plus the back-cover discography with genre notes. /for/ pages are compilations: each audience's stack as a tracklist with why each app is on it. /guides/ is a row of staff-pick shelf-talker cards that open into each guide. Catalogue numbers are computed in first_release order, so new apps append and old numbers never change.
styles.signatureInteraction: Face-out. Hovering or focusing a spine on desktop turns that record face-out: its flex-basis grows from 42px to 400px over 220ms and the sleeve face appears, while the previous face-out record turns back to its spine. On touch, a tap toggles it through a <button aria-expanded> in each spine, and the app name stays a plain link. Technique: a flex row with :hover, :focus-within and :has() collapses the default record while another is hovered; a .is-out class is kept by about 20 lines of JS; every sleeve face is server-rendered. No JS: the newest release is server-rendered face-out, every spine name is a link, and the back-cover discography directly below lists every tagline, so nothing is reachable only by interaction. Reduced motion: the swap is instant.
styles.motionGrammar: Records slide and nothing fades. Face-out 220ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). On load the newest record rises 12px and settles once over 300ms (skipped under reduced motion). Divider cards never move; no scroll reveals; the sticky divider strip simply docks.
styles.readModeVariant: Liner notes. A 120px cloudberry masthead band holds the roundel, the post's date and read time (Familjen 600 15px) and the title in Krona One at 40-48px, black, three lines at most at 1100px. Below sits the inner sleeve: a white sheet with the column in Familjen Grotesk 18/1.62 at 66ch, #141414, H2s in Familjen 600 at 26px, links underlined in black. The Quick Answer is the shrink-wrap sticker: a black panel titled 'Quick answer' in yellow, with the white 18px answer at the top of the sheet. Tables are back-cover tracklists: tabular figures, 1px black rules, no fills. Mentioned apps close the post face-out (sleeve with 'Open →'); on desktop their spine also stands in the right margin as a vertical link. The journal index is a 'Liner notes' tracklist by date. /transparency/ is 'Credits': one block per app (role and value in Apple's terms, plus source status), headed by the app's spine laid flat as a horizontal bar, never a coloured side border. The alternatives index is 'Versus', grouped under our app's flat spine bar. About is 'Pressed by one person'; support is 'The counter'; 404 is 'Not in the catalogue', followed by the shelf.
styles.assetsNeeded: A clean vector studio mark, also cut as a centre-label roundel; the PNG has a baked checkerboard. Data: per-app studio_swatch {ground, ink} for spines and sleeves (ink must reach 4.5:1 on its ground), sampled from icons now and replaced with each chosen microsite's ground. Optional later: per-app SVG wordmarks for sleeve faces. QR SVGs, icons and screenshots exist; spines, dividers and stickers are CSS.
styles.risk: Familiar: 'studio as record label' is a known indie trope, and the pick lands near where many studio redesigns go. Nineteen app colours on a yellow wall can turn noisy unless the swatch data is tuned. Vertical spine text scans slower than a list (the back-cover discography and mobile stack carry that load). Cloudberry plus black can read as a warning sign if the shelf is not the clear focus.
styles.memoryTest: A yellow record-shop wall with a shelf of nineteen spines in different colours. Every Lagerland app was a record; I touched one and it turned to face me, with sleeve, price sticker and a QR where the barcode goes.

styles.label: Page 100
styles.lineage: European broadcast teletext: Yle Teksti-TV (still on air in Finland) and BBC Ceefax (1974-2012), and its Level 1 grammar: a 40x24 character grid, seven colours on black, double-height rows, 2x3 block-mosaic graphics, three-digit page numbers with 100 as the index, four Fastext colour keys, and MIX mode, where text sits over the live TV picture.
styles.thesis: The studio is a teletext service. Every app, post and manifest has a three-digit page you can type, Fastext keys route the sections, and each app's own picture shows through in MIX. It refuses the hero-plus-card grid by making the homepage a P100 index.
styles.scene: A viewer on the sofa in a dark Finnish living room on an October evening, the TV's teletext page the only light in the room. Scheme: dark.
styles.colorStrategy: Full palette, each teletext colour with one job: yellow for titles and date, cyan for links and page numbers, green for declared data and prices, white for frame text, and blue for band rows (only behind text). Red, green, yellow and cyan are the Fastext keys; magenta is reserved for the current page number. No glow, scanlines or CRT curvature.

palette.role: CRT black: ground and text boxes
reading white: column body text (14.9:1); frame text is #FFFFFF
teletext yellow: titles, date and clock, Fastext 3
teletext cyan: links, page numbers, Fastext 4
teletext green: declared values (0, false, None), prices, Fastext 2
teletext blue: band rows behind white or yellow text only, never as text (2.4:1)
teletext red: Fastext 1, 404 (5.25:1 on black; black on red for key fields)

type.text: Radio Canada Big 400, 600 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 11 KB each)
type.utility: none: Tiny5 covers the real data (page numbers, clock, plist keys)
type.rationale: Among Fontsource faces, Tiny5's blocky caps and stepped diagonals sit closest to the SAA5050 teletext character generator. It sets the header row, page numbers and double-height titles (transform: scaleY(2), a real teletext gesture) and never sets running text. Radio Canada Big is the open typeface made for a public broadcaster (CBC/Radio-Canada), with open apertures for screens: the broadcaster's voice for the reading column and app lines. Total about 42 KB.

styles.conversion: The index is the routing: each need-line links to /apps/<slug>/, and its page number works as a typed shortcut (201-219 go to microsites; 501-604 go to alternatives pages, which wear their app's world). Selecting a line (hover or focus) puts that app on air behind the page (MIX) and fills the subtitle panel: tagline, price.value verbatim in green, a cyan 'Go to 207 Observa', the official App Store badge (unaltered, on its own black box) and, on desktop, the app's QR in a white quiet-zone box. Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The sticky bar is the Fastext row (fixed at the bottom on mobile; the last grid row stays fixed on desktop). Smart App Banner: only on journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons are never redrawn into mosaic. The teletext frame stays uniform on purpose, and each app's art appears only as itself, in full colour: as the MIX picture and as the 28px squircle chip on mobile lines.

styles.navigation: Three systems, all plain links underneath. The header row shows where you stand (the current page number in magenta). The Fastext row of four coloured keys is on every page: red Apps 200, green Journal 300, yellow Transparency 400, cyan Index 100; on posts, red and green become previous and next. The keypad takes any three-digit page on any page; on desktop you can type digits anywhere outside a field, and the header counter rolls. Page map, computed by Liquid in ascending date order so numbers never change: 100 home; 200 /apps/ (201-219 microsites); 301-342 journal; 400 transparency; 500-699 alternatives; 700 guides (701-705); 710 /for/ (711-714); 800 about; 810 support.
styles.signatureInteraction: Page search plus MIX. Typing three digits (anywhere on desktop, or in the keypad field on touch) makes the header counter roll 'P2--', 'P20-', 'P207', and the page goes, as on a TV. Hovering or focusing an index line switches MIX on: the black ground drops away and that app's own icon art fills the screen behind boxed text. Technique: a vanilla JS keydown listener (ignored inside inputs and with modifier keys) reads a Liquid-rendered JSON map of page number to URL. MIX is pure CSS: :has(.line:is(:hover,:focus-visible)) swaps a background layer whose image is each line's inline --pic custom property. No JS: lines are plain links, the keypad field is not rendered (it is an enhancement, not content), and MIX still works through CSS. Reduced motion: the counter shows the final number at once, and MIX is already instant.
styles.motionGrammar: Teletext has no easing: everything changes on a frame. On first load, once per session and only under html.js, rows arrive top to bottom in about 12 frames over 400ms, like a page being received; content is server-rendered visible, and the effect only replays it. The header counter rolls while digits are typed, the clock ticks seconds, and the cursor blinks in 1s steps. No fades, slides, glow or parallax. Reduced motion: no row arrival, the clock shows minutes without ticking, and the cursor is steady.

The Fastext row sits at the foot, sticky on mobile: red previous, green next, yellow section index, cyan 100. The alternatives index is P500, results-style lines grouped under our app's name. Guides are P701-705, /for/ is P711-714, about P800, support P810. 404 reads 'PAGE NOT IN SERVICE' with the header counter still searching, followed by the P100 index.
styles.assetsNeeded: A clean vector studio mark, plus a hand-authored 2x3 block-mosaic version of the star mark and of the LAGERLAND wordmark (SVG or CSS grid; a small vector task). Data: a per-app index_line front-matter field (28 characters or fewer, the need phrase on P100) and the Liquid page-number map. MIX uses the existing 1024px icons; screenshots and QR SVGs exist.
styles.risk: Retro-broadcast nostalgia is strong in Finland, the UK and Europe but unknown to many US visitors. A pixel face and seven full-saturation colours tip into 8-bit costume if Tiny5 ever reaches running text or headings in Read mode. The dark-only column carries 15-minute posts, and MIX over busy icon art (WanderWiki) needs every line boxed. The 'receive-only' idea must apply to the apps' declared network calls only, never to the website, which runs GoatCounter.
styles.memoryTest: The Lagerland site was a teletext page: 'P100 LAGERLAND' in the corner, yellow double-height titles, an index of apps with page numbers. I typed 207 and it jumped to Observa, and when I hovered a line, that app's icon came on air behind the text.

canon: Canon (the owner's standing exit, played straight, never recommended): the indie Apple studio page at the craft level of Panic's and The Iconfactory's sites. White ground and an SF-like grotesk; headline beside floating iPhone/Mac mockups; a short trust row; a 3-column grid of app tiles (icon, name, one line, App Store badge) grouped by category; a featured-app band; a privacy strip linking /transparency/; journal cards; FAQ; footer.
notes: Honest ranking, made before mapping: 1 record label (most resonant; carries non-flattening, routing and proof), 2 räsymatto, 3 stamps and first-day cover, 4 orienteering, 5 teletext, 6 63°N almanac, 7 open depot (the name's literal reading, so last). The dice mapped A = candidate 7 (THE ROLL) and C = candidate 5 (SECOND ROLL, re-roll 1), and B = candidate 1 as IMPECCABLE'S PICK. The three styles differ in world (depot, record shop, broadcast), topology (aisle ledger with pull-out drawers; horizontal spine shelf with face-out accordion; numbered pages with keypad and MIX) and lighting (cool white-lit Committed, drenched cloudberry, dark Full palette). Every face was verified with npm view and npm pack against @fontsource 5.3.0, latin static woff2: Big Shoulders Stencil Display, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, Martian Mono, Krona One, Familjen Grotesk, Tiny5, Radio Canada Big; all page budgets are under 90 KB. Shared data dependency for all three: a per-app studio_swatch {ground, ink} (or the chosen microsite's tokens), so the studio shows each app in its own world colours, plus the computed catalogue order by release.first_release. Copy guard: AppMeta Pulse ships no Privacy Manifest yet, so studio copy says 'declared data' and '18 manifests + 1 pending', never 'NSPrivacyTracking false x19'. Findings for the build phase: the studio mark PNG has a baked checkerboard; seven icons have baked white corners and mediakit.png is non-square; the site runs GoatCounter, so the studio must not claim to be untracked; alternatives/index.html hard-codes numberOfItems 104; the Smart App Banner could be emitted on single-app journal posts and guides. Tare (status upcoming) stays off the studio until the owner lists it; if listed, A shows an empty labelled bin, B an unprinted sleeve with only the cartouche ('LGL 020 forthcoming'), and C a 'page in preparation' line.
